newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican business seeks lid on utility rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Mexican business seeks lid on utility rate rises.

text.p: Mexico's private sector is seeking a temporary halt to rate rises in public sector goods and services, a top business leader said, though he acknowledged there could be minimal increases.

In a report in Reforma newspaper on Sunday, Hector Larios Santillan, head of the Business Coordinating Council, was quoted as outlining some of the private sector's demands if it is to renew a wage-price pact with government and labor.
"The government needs to continue along the route of stimulating the private sector, and under those circumstances we demand that tariffs on its goods and services not be raised," he said.

"If it decides to increase them, let it be by the minimum amount, and always in exchange for more efficiency in delivering them," he added at an Employers Confederation (Coparmex) conference in Ensanada, Baja California.

Mexico's Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles has said that electricity prices are badly lagging inflation and need to be increased. Rates on other services like water and gasoline are usually adjusted upwards in the annual revisions of the government's anti-inflation wage-price pacts.

The current arrangement, known as the Alliance for Economic Recovery, expires at the end of this month, and business, government and labor leaders are currently debating under what terms it should be renewed or revised.
